who: Historian of modern Europe and Germany, University of Toronto Scarborough, DPhil Oxford.

evidence.says: The author biography in this December 2008 publication identifies Modris Eksteins as a Toronto Scarborough history professor with BPhil and DPhil degrees from Oxford.
The authority for Eksteins, Modris cites Nineteenth-century Germany (1983), identifying him as professor of history at the University of Toronto.

notes: The candidate authority, Toronto affiliation in the relevant period, historical field and Oxford doctorate agree.

who: Historian of eighteenth-century Britain and diplomacy, University of Toronto, DPhil Worcester College, Oxford, 1992.

evidence.says: The contributor biography states that Jennifer Mori took her DPhil at Worcester College, Oxford, in 1992 and has taught at Toronto since 1996.
The authority identifies the author of William Pitt and the French Revolution and The Culture of Diplomacy; the latter source describes her as an associate professor at Toronto.

notes: The exact Oxford college, Toronto career and publications connect the supervisor to the candidate authority.

who: Historian of modern European Jewish history, University of Chicago, DPhil modern history, Oxford, 1974.

evidence.says: Chicago identifies Wasserstein as its emeritus professor of modern European Jewish history and records a 1974 DPhil in modern history from Nuffield College, Oxford.
The authority for Wasserstein, Bernard cites a 2014 publication identifying him as professor of modern European Jewish history at Chicago since 2003.

notes: The candidate authority explicitly places him at Chicago across both dissertation years, and the Oxford doctorate matches.

who: Ian K. Steele, historian of the British Atlantic and early North America, University of Western Ontario.

evidence.says: The authority expands Ian K. Steele to Ian Kenneth Steele, also records the form Ian Steele, and identifies him as a Western Ontario history professor; a 2003 conference there celebrated his retirement.
Western History remembers Ian Steele as a departmental colleague and graduate mentor, identifying The English Atlantic (1986) among his influential works.

notes: The authority directly connects the abbreviated and full names to the same Western historian. The London doctorate was not independently verified; retirement does not preclude earlier supervision of later-completing students.

who: Anne Kelly Knowles, historical geographer, University of Maine History, PhD geography, Wisconsin-Madison, 1993.

evidence.says: Knowles records a 1993 geography PhD from Wisconsin-Madison and joining Maine History in August 2015; the page lists Calvinists Incorporated and Past Time, Past Place.

Her 2020 CV lists Gregory Gaines as a supervised History PhD candidate studying Swedish immigration and Justus Hillebrand as a co-supervised History PhD candidate with the listed land-and-agricultural-knowledge project.
The authority names Anne Kelly Knowles as the geographer and author/editor of Calvinists Incorporated and Past Time, Past Place.

notes: The full name, doctorate, Maine appointment and both named advisees establish the match.

who: Robert S. Starobin, historian of slavery and African American history, University of Wisconsin-Madison; PhD UC Berkeley.

evidence.says: The authority identifies Robert S. Starobin as an assistant professor of history at Wisconsin-Madison, author of Industrial Slavery in the Old South, and holder of a UC Berkeley PhD.
The department history credits Robert Starobin with introducing African American history into its curriculum during his brief teaching career.

notes: The candidate authority and department history identify the same Madison historian in the relevant field. Dissertation completion years alone do not establish continued faculty service.

who: Jean Comaroff, historical anthropologist, formerly University of Chicago and subsequently Harvard.

evidence.says: The department lists Dingley’s 2018 joint History dissertation with J. Comaroff and E. Osborn starred as co-chairs, separately listing J.L. Comaroff on the committee.
Harvard identifies Jean Comaroff as a former Chicago anthropology professor, there until 2012, and author of Body of Power, Spirit of Resistance.
The authority for Comaroff, Jean identifies her through Body of Power, Spirit of Resistance.

notes: Match Jean (p-1897), not John (p-1898; LC n80137823). Chicago distinguishes the two committee members; her move in 2012 is compatible with later completion of an existing advisee’s dissertation.

who: Richard Connors, historian of Britain and empire, University of Ottawa.

evidence.says: The approval page for Martin Hubley’s Ottawa History PhD, Desertion, Identity and the Experience of Authority in the North American Squadron of the Royal Navy, names Richard Connors as thesis supervisor.

The authority for Connors, Richard cites Anglo-American Millennialism (2004), identifying him as an assistant professor of history at Ottawa, and also identifies him as an editor of Hanoverian Britain and Empire.
Ottawa lists Richard Connors among its faculty researching European history.

notes: A listed student’s thesis directly identifies the supervisor; the candidate authority places the same historian at Ottawa before the dissertation years.
